rules.text: French e-invoicing reform: from 1 Sep 2026 all companies must be able to receive e-invoices, and large and mid-size companies must issue them. From 1 Sep 2027 SMEs and micro-enterprises must issue them. The scheme concerns businesses established in France.

For tax, an invoice may be written in a foreign language, and the administration may require a certified translation for a control (not systematic). Separate language-law issue: the Toubon law (art. 2) requires French on invoices for consumers and end-user business buyers in France. Exchanges between professionals who buy to resell, and export operations, are outside it. Where French is required, a translation is allowed if the French version is as legible as the foreign one (art. 4).

bilingual.condition: French at least as legible as the other language

rules.notes: Read: a French law-firm article (kohenavocats.fr, 2026-11-23) that quotes CGI art. 289 IV and 54, the Toubon law art. 2 and 4, the 1996 circular, and Court of Cassation rulings; and BOFiP/service-public excerpts from search results. The statutes and BOFiP pages themselves were not read in full. The firm says the safest choice for a French end-user customer is a French or bilingual invoice, and that the question for a French professional end user is not settled by the cases it consulted. Our bilingual layout prints both languages in the same type size.

source.title: CGI annexe II, art. 242 nonies A (Legifrance)

rules.text: VAT-law mandatory particulars on a French invoice (art. 242 nonies A, I): full name, registration number and address of seller and customer; seller VAT ID; issue date; a unique number in a chronological, continuous sequence; delivery address if different; per line quantity, precise description, unit price excl. VAT and the VAT rate or the exemption; whether the operations are goods only, services only or both; discounts; date of supply if different from issue date; tax per rate with totals excl. VAT; for an exemption, the relevant provision or a statement that the operation is exempt; 'Autoliquidation' when the buyer owes the VAT; 'Autofacturation' for self-billing; 'Option pour le paiement de la taxe d'apres les debits' when opted. Invoices up to 150 EUR excl. VAT may omit the seller's individual VAT number and the exemption reference (II).
rules.notes: Read from Legifrance on 2026-11-25. This is only the VAT-law list. Commercial-law particulars (payment due date, late-payment penalty, 40 EUR recovery indemnity, SIREN-based data) come from Code de commerce L441-9, which has not been read, so the French pack stays held for issuing. Not tax advice. RE-VERIFY BY 2026-12-31 (held automatically from 2027-01-01): the legal basis of these particulars, CGI art. 289, is repealed from 1 January 2027 by Ordonnance 2025-1247 and replaced in the CIBS (art. L216-33), which leaves the exact particulars to a decree not yet read. The annexe II art. 242 nonies A page read shows no repeal notice, and the BOFiP note BOI-RES-TVA-000253 (administration guidance, secondary source, 7 Oct 2026) says invoice rules continue under the CGI and that CGI references on invoices stay accepted until 30 June 2028. That is not enough to verify the 2027 rules, so the pack asks for a re-read instead of assuming either way.
anchors: Un numéro unique basé sur une séquence chronologique et continue

rules.text: Commercial-law particulars for a French B2B invoice (L441-9 I): names and addresses of the parties (and billing address if different), date of sale or service, quantity, precise description and unit price excl. VAT, any acquired price reduction, the date by which payment is due, the discount terms for early payment, the rate of the penalties due the day after the payment date, the fixed recovery-cost indemnity due on late payment, and the purchase-order number when the buyer set one. Administrative fine up to 75,000 EUR (natural person) or 375,000 EUR (company); doubled on repeat within two years (II).
rules.notes: Read from Legifrance on 2026-11-25 (version in force since 26 Apr 2019). The tool does not yet hold payment due date, early-payment discount terms, late-penalty rate or the indemnity amount, so France stays held for issuing. Adding those fields is the step that opens France. The 40 EUR amount is not in this article and is not encoded here.
anchors: La facture mentionne la date à laquelle le règlement doit intervenir
indemnité forfaitaire pour frais de recouvrement

rules.text: The French government business portal lists mandatory invoice particulars for every invoice: issue date, unique sequential number, date of supply, seller identity (company name, SIREN, registered address, legal form), buyer identity, purchase-order number when set by the buyer, seller VAT ID (and the business buyer's), description with quantity, unit price excl. VAT and VAT rate or exemption, totals excl. and incl. VAT, any price reduction, the payment due date, early-payment discount terms, the late-payment penalty rate and the 40 euro recovery indemnity (for business buyers). From 1 September 2026 four new particulars phase in: buyer SIREN for business buyers, delivery address if different, nature of the operation, and the option-for-debits note.

source.title: CGI annexe II art. 242 nonies A and Code de commerce L441-9 (Legifrance)

rules.text: A French invoice must carry the particulars of CGI annexe II art. 242 nonies A (VAT law) and Code de commerce L441-9 (commercial law): seller and buyer names and addresses, the seller's registration number and VAT ID, issue date, unique sequential number, per line quantity, precise description, unit price excl. VAT and VAT rate or exemption, discounts, date of supply, totals per rate, the exemption reference when exempt, and the payment due date, early-payment discount terms, late-penalty rate and recovery-cost indemnity. The tool holds an invoice until every one of those it can check is present.
rules.notes: Built from two articles read on Legifrance on 2026-11-25. Every payment value is entered by the seller, nothing is defaulted (the 40 EUR indemnity figure is not in L441-9, so it is the seller's entry). Not enforced because the tool cannot know it: delivery address, goods or services nature, and the 'Autoliquidation' and debit-option mentions beyond what the exemption-note check covers; a French business buyer's registration number is required and Amazon data does not supply it, so invoices to French buyers are held. The newest version of art. 242 nonies A applies from 1 Sept 2026, or 1 Sept 2027 for micro and small and medium businesses; the tool does not know the seller's size and asks for the union of particulars. Credit notes and corrections are NOT covered (FR correction rules unread), so FR corrections stay held. Not tax advice. Source monitoring watches the 242 nonies A page only; L441-9 is at https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000038414397 (rule FR-COMM-L441-9). RE-VERIFY BY 2026-12-31 (held automatically from 2027-01-01): the legal basis of these particulars, CGI art. 289, is repealed from 1 January 2027 by Ordonnance 2025-1247 and replaced in the CIBS (art. L216-33), which leaves the exact particulars to a decree not yet read. The annexe II art. 242 nonies A page read shows no repeal notice, and the BOFiP note BOI-RES-TVA-000253 (administration guidance, secondary source, 7 Oct 2026) says invoice rules continue under the CGI and that CGI references on invoices stay accepted until 30 June 2028. That is not enough to verify the 2027 rules, so the pack asks for a re-read instead of assuming either way.

source.title: CGI art. 289, I-5 (version in force 31 Dec 2023 to 31 Dec 2026)

rules.text: Any document or message that modifies the initial invoice and refers to it specifically and unequivocally is treated as an invoice, and must carry all the particulars required for an invoice (CGI art. 289 I-5).
rules.notes: Read on Legifrance 2026-11-25. Ordonnance 2025-1247 repeals CGI art. 289 from 1 January 2027 (recodified into the CIBS, not yet read), so this rule must be re-verified by 2026-12-31 and French corrections are held automatically from 2027-01-01 until then. The text read does not say how credit notes or tax-amount changes are treated, so they stay refused for France. Whether a correction changes VAT owed is a tax decision this tool does not make. Nothing here is tax advice. Update 2026-11-25: per ordonnance 2025-1247 art. 15 table (primary), art. 289 I-5 is not kept in force and is repealed on 2027-01-01. Its replacement is CIBS L216-25 and L216-26, whose particulars depend on a decree not yet published, so the safety hold from 2027-01-01 stays.
anchors: Tout document ou message qui modifie la facture initiale
fait référence à la facture initiale de façon spécifique et non équivoque

source.title: CIBS arts. L216-25, L216-26, L216-33 (Sous-section 2: Factures), version of 1 January 2027, as created by Ordonnance 2026-671

rules.text: From 1 January 2027 French VAT invoicing moves into the CIBS. This does not by itself invalidate existing invoice rules. L216-25: a document that refers to an invoice specifically and unequivocally and modifies it is also an invoice. L216-26: a corrective invoice replaces or removes wrong elements or adds omitted ones. L216-33: the invoice carries the particulars of art. L224-3 items 1 to 4 and other elements useful for managing or checking the tax; a decree sets the exact particulars. That decree text is not read yet.
rules.notes: Read on Legifrance 2026-11-25 (page marked 'A venir', version of 1 Jan 2027). The CIBS leaves the exact list of invoice particulars to a decree, and also leaves to a decree the rules on rectifications, foreign currency and foreign language. Until that decree is read, French invoices and corrections cannot be verified for dates from 2027-01-01, so the existing French gate rules end on 2026-12-31 and hold automatically. This rule changes no behaviour by itself. Nothing is tax advice. Secondary pointer, not relied on: BOFiP BOI-RES-TVA-000253-20261007 (https://bofip.impots.gouv.fr/bofip/14901-PGP.html/identifiant%3DBOI-RES-TVA-000253-20261007) says the recodification is at constant law and invoice format and e-transmission rules stay under the CGI from 2027. Ordonnance 2025-1247 art. 46 (https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000054587035, in force since 29 July 2026) was read on 2026-11-25: it only says that references to CGI VAT provisions in existing laws, administrative acts, invoices and contracts mean the CIBS provisions that replace them, and that this also covers invoices and contracts that produce effects until 30 June 2028. It does not say which particulars an invoice issued in 2027 must carry, so the re-verify date stays. Decree search 2026-11-25: no implementing decree found. Secondary sources (altermes.fr, squairlaw.com, legifiscal.fr, dated Jan to Oct 2026) say the decree is still to be published, and that CGI references stay valid on invoices until 30 June 2028 (ordonnance 2025-1247 art. 46 II as moved by ordonnance 2026-671 art. 17; BOI-RES-TVA-000253). Secondary only, not relied on. Not checked on Legifrance/JORF directly. 2026-11-25 policy wording: the hold on French gate rules from 2027-01-01 is an InvoiceGuard SAFETY HOLD pending the implementing decree. It is NOT France invalidating existing invoice rules on 1 January 2027. PRIMARY, read on Legifrance 2026-11-25: Ordonnance 2025-1247 art. 46 (https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000053100905, in force since 29 July 2026): II extends reading CGI VAT references as CIBS references to invoices and contracts producing effects until 30 June 2028. That covers REFERENCES only, it does not say which particulars rules apply. CIBS L216-33 (in force 2027-01-01) provides for a decree on particulars: https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/id/LEGISCTA000054525411/2027-01-01 . SECONDARY (administrative doctrine, not a statute), BOI-RES-TVA-000253-20261007 para 2.2: VAT regulations in annexes II, III and IV to the CGI stay applicable until the replacing CIBS regulations enter into force; para 2.3 says the same for regulatory provisions currently in legislative form. Not yet confirmed from primary text for CGI art. 289 itself (FR-CORR-289) or art. 242 nonies A. No final implementing decree verified either way. Until a primary source confirms continuity, the safety hold stays. PRIMARY, read 2026-11-25 (https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/loda/id/JORFTEXT000053091516/ art. 15 table, as modified by ordonnance 2026-671): the CGI provisions kept in force until reprise by regulation include '3 du I, IV et VII de l'article 289' and art. 289 bis. Paragraph I-5 of art. 289 (the correction text) is NOT in that table, so it is repealed from 2027-01-01 and replaced by CIBS L216-25 and L216-26 (read, see text). Annex II to the CGI (art. 242 nonies A) is a regulation outside this table, no primary statement on its continuity read yet.
